abstract: The motion planning problem is a fundamental challenge in the field of robotics. This study presents a novel sampling-based pathfinding algorithm that enables robot to navigate complicated terrain by providing obstacle avoidance and local trajectory planning. Sampling-based pathfinding algorithms have been extensively utilized in motion planning challenges. The method has several limitations, including a sluggish convergence rate, significant variation in search time, a vast and dense sample space, and non-smooth search routes. This study introduces RE-RRT* (Robust and Efficient RRT*), an enhanced version of the sampling-based pathfinding algorithm designed to efficiently discover a rapid path that is nearly optimal. RE-RRT* iteratively improves the path by utilizing the Choose Parent and Rewire processes. As the random tree expands, the sample space becomes restricted, resulting in a reduction in unnecessary searches. Simulation demonstrate that the RE-RRT<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> algorithm is capable of achieving smoother and more efficient convergence to a shorter path with fewer iterations, even in the presence of various obstacles. The proposed approach can enhance search efficacy, expedite convergence, and reduce processing time. Due to these factors, our proposed RE-RRT<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> algorithm has superior performance compared to previous sample-based algorithms in terms of stability, speed, computing time, and sampling space.

articleTitle: A Comparison of EKF and PF to Localize an Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (AUV) using Inertial Navigation System
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Using inertial navigation techniques, the position of an autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) has been estimated in this research. The Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) and the Particle Filter (PF) are the two filters that have been employed to deduce the AUV's location. The EKF technique relies on linearizing a system's state space equation using the current values of the state parameters. The Particle Filter (PF) relies on the repetitive calculation of pertinent probability distributions through the utilisation of substantial sampling and intermittent stochastic measures. These two filters are implemented using a nonlinear kinetic model of a sample AUV, and the results of the position estimation of the two filters are compared. The findings indicate that, despite the simplifications made in the linearization process, the results obtained using the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) are more accurate in representing the actual trajectory of the vehicle compared to the estimations obtained using the Particle Filter (PF).

articleTitle: Design of Winch System with Automated Cable Winding Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Winch mechanism is employed to wi<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>d/unwind a cable and the resulting tension is used to lift or deploy the load being powered manually or by an automated system. In the past, people have been manually lifting loads, powered, by a crank used to wind up or out a line. Research and technical advancements in winch systems have made the winching process more efficient, and the required time for retrieval and deployment is also reduced. In recent years, technology has evolved exponentially, allowing designers to create better, more compact systems to meet required functional needs. This research study explores the different design considerations of an automated cable winding winch mechanism which includes the selection of motors, gears and gear ratios, shafts, shaft keys, cable diameter, and winding speed. The selection of these was based on design calculations optimized through multiple iterations. The resulting model was analyzed for structural stability under dynamic and static loading. The stress and strain generated under the applied loads were within the yield stress and strain of the design. Results were further verified by developing a scaled-down prototype of the model and testing it by applying various loading conditions. However, the scope of our research does not end here. It contributes to assisting the research on more compact and lighter designs that could be achieved by using variable frequency drive (VFD) technology.

articleTitle: Classification and Segmentation of Gastroenterology Images Using Saliency Mapping in Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This research work has been done towards the treatment of Gastrointestinal (GI) Cancer by experimenting as to how a computer aided design can help oncologists classify and segment GI Cancer using Gastroenterology (GE) Images. The concept of Attention Module by the name of Convolution Block Attention Module (CBAM) using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) layers has been utilized to achieve saliency mapping in these images. The different layers of the CNN are tweaked and the hyper parameters are consistently checked and changed to achieve maximum accuracy. The CBAM Algorithm is divided into Channel Attention (CA) and Spatial Attention (SA) module. The Channel Attention has been implemented in the HSV Color Space for finding the best color space for segmentation purposes of the Chromo endoscopy medical images. Classification, followed by segmentation, is again implemented using CNN based model for normal and abnormal cancer images. For classification, 92% test accuracy has been achieved, while 70% Dice Similarity Coefficient has been obtained for segmentation. The results achieved are competitive as compared to the previous reported results on the GE images dataset.

articleTitle: Thermal Modelling of the Selective Laser Melting (SLM) 3D Printing Process and Melt Pool Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The purpose of this research is to develop a 2D mathematical model to obtain the thermal characteristics of Selective Laser Melting (SLM) 3D Printing Process. In SLM, metal powder is spread on a build surface (usually preheated) and laser melts the powders in selective regions and consolidates it i.e. changes the powder into densely packed metal in selective regions. In this way selective powder layers are added in the z-direction which eventually results in a 3D part. The transient heat conduction equation with surface heating was solved in 2D to simulate the x-y (width) and y-z (depth) planes and obtain the melt pool dimensions. The thermal profile was also obtained in the cases of Ti6Al4V and Steel 304. Lastly, the thermal profile was modelled in the case of Ti6Al4V powder in SLM and the melt pool width and depth were predicted and compared to some available experimental data.

articleTitle: FMI for Sharing NASTRAN Dynamic FEM models
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This paper presents an approach for sharing dynamic FEM structure models built in NASTRAN environment through the Functional Mock-up Interface (FMI) standard. Relevant data such as stiffness and mass matrices is generated in HDF5 database from modal analysis solution without the need for altering of NASTRAN solution sequence. State space Linear Time Invariant (LTI) model is generated from this dataset which represents the dynamics of structure model in modal coordinates. Nodal accelerations, displacements and elemental stresses can be output from FMI model by constructing the output matrix from eigenvectors and modal stress contribution data at desired element IDs. Generated FMI model is simulated in Simulink and is compared with NASTRAN modal transient solution which shows good correlation.

articleTitle: Selection of Suitable Internal Control Gene for Analyzing Innate and Humoral Immune Responses in COVID-19 Gene Expression Studies
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Background and Objectives: Gene expression analysis is crucial in order to develop new diagnostic and prognostic markers. Selection of internal control gene is critical step for accurate assessment of quantitative real time PCR (qRT-PCR) results. The accuracy of gene analysis depends on accurate normalization of mRNA fractions using well-expressed genes. This method compensates for errors caused during experimental design. These genes are called internal control or housekeeping genes. Depending upon their constitutive expression at relatively high levels housekeeping genes have traditionally been used for normalization, although often without any proper validation. Fewer studies have been conducted to estimate the suitable housekeeping genes for the expression studies of novel corona virus. A case control study was conducted to identify suitable internal control gene for covid-19 gene expression analysis and to use selected internal control gene to better understand the cross talk between cytokines mediated immune response in host infected by novel corona virus. Materials and Methods: Expression of internal control genes GAPDH and SDHA using qRT-PCR was analyzed for 100 healthy controls and 136 COVID-19 confirmed cases. Statistical algorithms such as Bestkeeper, GeNorm, Delta CT and comprehensive gene stability approaches were used for the selection of suitable internal control gene against 12 genes of innate and immune host response (interferon <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> & <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>, Interleukin-1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha, 1-\beta, 4,6,7,10,11,13,15$</tex>, and 27) in SARS CoV-19 infection. Results: GAPDH was found to be significantly more consistent in expression as compared to SDHA both in case group and control group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(p < 0.001)$</tex>. Statistical approaches have shown stable expression of GAPDH as well with M value 1.1. Conclusions: Our data revealed a notable difference in the expression levels between internal controls (GAPDH & SDHA) in both COVID-19 patients and healthy individuals. This underlines the necessity for thorough validation of internal controls prior to their utilization in quantitative assays.

articleTitle: Shock and Vibration Analysis (FEA) of Electronic Cabinets Onboard Naval Platforms
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In marine platforms, it is imperative to isolate cabinets containing onboard electronics from shock and vibration experienced during its operation to increase their operational life. This paper is aimed at shock and vibration analysis of said cabinets providing their load bearing, optimum damping, and stiffness values for design optimization of vibration isolators. FEA results were then validated using empirical formulation.

articleTitle: Effect of Variation in Diameter on the Rotation of Half Submerged Wave Driven Savonius Turbines – An Experimental Investigation
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Ocean wave energy is a promising field for renewable energy. Turbine is a major challenge area for economy of this field. An interest in using turbines directly for wave energy conversion has been increasing recently as turbines have been used successfully to harness the energy of flow throughout history. However, the field of dynamics of a wave driven turbine is vastly unexplored. This study focuses on experimentally investigating the effects of variation in the diameter of Savonius type of turbines on their rotation while they are driven by identical waves and rotate freely. A total of seven turbines with a diameter between 0.013m and 0.080m were tested on identical waves with a height of 0.030m. It was generally noted that the motion of all the turbines was synchronised with that of the driving wave cycles. The turbines having a diameter smaller than wave height exhibited a predominantly continuous rotational motion with a fluctuating speed. Furthermore, a decrease in the fluctuation was noted with increasing moment of inertia of the turbine.

articleTitle: Forecasting Particulate Matter (PM 2.5) Concentration in Air with Double Attention GRU
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Accurate PM2.5 concentration forecasting is crucial for reducing air pollution, protecting public health, directing urban development choices, and learning more about the effects of climate change. This research examines the Beijing multisite dataset to assess air quality based on PM2.5 concentrations. The air pollutant dataset is preprocessed. Feature engineering is carried out by utilizing a min-max scaler to handle the nonlinear correlation between attributes. The gated recurrent unit (GRU) with the attention mechanism has been exploited for PM2.5 concentration. GRUs excel in handling time series data based on their ability to capture long-term dependencies and temporal patterns, addressing the vanishing gradient issue. The integration of the attention mechanism is vital as it enables the model to concentrate on pertinent segments of the input sequence to enhance the predictive performance by capturing essential temporal dependencies and features. The model's generalization and reliability are assessed through multi-hour prediction with window sizes of 6, 8, and 12 and achieve the highest performance in terms of error measure RMSE, MAE, and R2score, with normalized and unnormalized datasets.

articleTitle: Alkaline Earth Metal-Modified Cellulose Triacetate: A Promising Advancement in Battery Separator Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Cellulose triacetate (CTA) has emerged as promising material used as separators in Zinc Silver battery due to its excellent thermal stability, high mechanical strength and good electrolyte wettability. This paper explores the modification of CTA with alkaline earth metals, specifically Mg, Ca and Ba to further enhance its properties and efficiency in Zinc Silver battery systems. Through systematic analysis and experimentation, the impact of alkaline earth metal incorporation on the structural and electrochemical performance of CTA. Employing 1:1 molar ratio of silver nitrate and each alkaline earth metal (Mg, Ca & Ba), we systematically analyzed modified CTAs using FT-IR, Thermo gravimetric analysis (TGA), Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and AASs techniques. FT-IR analysis reveals notable shifts in functional group vibrations as appearance of band at 310cm-1, 301cm-1 and 353cm-1 corresponds to Mg, Ca and Ba respectively indicating successful incorporation of metals into CTA moiety. TGA analysis demonstrates enhanced thermal stability of metal modified CTA indicating its potential for reliable performance. SEM images highlights a refined morphology with enhanced interconnectivity, indicative of improved structural integrity and ion transport pathways in metal-modified CTA leading to enhance cycleability. AAS measurement confirms the presence of metal ions within the cellulose triacetate matrix amounting 2880, 3690 and 3060 ppm of Mg, Ca and Ba respectively, validating the successful modification process. Additionally, their electrochemical performance in zinc silver battery through charge-discharge profile and efficiency measurement of cell was assessed. Remarkably it is revealed that magnesium-modified CTA demonstrates superior performance among the tested metals, exhibits charge-discharge profile up to 8 cycle study having 28% efficiency, showcasing its robust stability and promising longevity for advancing battery separator technology.

articleTitle: A Secure and Distributed Decision Based Handover Scheme for Low Earth Orbit Satellites in 6G Internet
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The space Internet offers wireless communication services at any location and anytime. Therefore, satellite communication plays a vital role in the 6G internet. However, the rapid movement of LEO satellites leads to quick transfers between ground stations. Previous research has focused on increasing authentication security ahead of handover while minimizing signalling and computation complexity. The rapid movement of satellites could lead to signaling problems and potential security risks at handover operation. Efficient and secure LEO satellite handover operation is essential to achieve broad coverage in 6G internet. This study proposes a secure and decentralized LEO satellite handover mechanism with ground stations. In the approach, LEO satellites make predictable decisions based on predictable trajectory, signal strength, and link reliability. Following predicted decisions, blockchain applications are utilized to accomplished a secure handover mechanism. The generated simulation outcomes demonstrate that the proposed scheme effectively manages the handover of LEO satellites to a different ground station in satellite communication. The performance analysis demonstrates less computing cost and signal overhead in handover operation.

articleTitle: Optimizing Electric Ducted Fan Performance (EDF): A Computational Design & Analysis Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Electric propulsion systems, such as Electric Ducted Fans (EDFs), a promising technology in the aerospace industry, offer compact and efficient solutions for propelling aircraft and VTOL vehicles. Despite notable advancements and model devel-opments, the design of EDFs remains a formidable challenge. Analytical methods provide valuable insights into underlying physics, however, their efficacy in predicting performance and stall characteristics is limited. Conversely, computational methods offer greater predictive capability but navigating the design process proves arduous and iterative. This paper proposed a hybrid approach to address this challenge by streamlining the analytical tools with computational tools. In the hybrid approach, systematic exploration begins by creating a CAD model using initially selected parameters. This model undergoes CFD analysis to generate a design matrix, allowing for the exploration of the most suitable parameters. For the case study, Initially two critical parameters—thrust and diameter—are selected for a small EDF tailored for UAV, representing performance and dimensional constraints, respectively, for selecting other parameters. The validity of this approach is verified through experimentation on the final 78% efficient design, targeting 19N thrust with a 120mm diameter.

articleTitle: Designing an Optimal Tuned Mass Damper System for Seismic Vibrations
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Earthquake jolts are synonymous with a system under forced vibration over a short period of time. A Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) is installed onto a building to minimize the effect of these vibrations by optimizing its mass, stiffness, and damping constant. A high-rise building subjected to seismic loads is isolated and simulated on ANSYS to derive the optimized TMD parameters. Simulations are run based on the effect of a lateral force on the building using response spectra from the 1940 Imperial Valley earthquake. The vibration response is mitigated by adding a Tuned Mass Damper at the top end of the building. A mathematical model is built to fit the desired response using second order differential equations. This 2 Degree of Freedom system with optimized values of stiffness (k) and damping coefficient (c) can be extrapolated for multistory buildings, based on the location of the TMD, building's natural frequency, and finely tuned TMD parameters. The paper investigates and calibrates the above-mentioned variables and validates the results analytically, numerically, and through simulations.

articleTitle: Accelerating Genome Sequence Analysis via Pre-Alignment Filtering: A Review of Sneaky Snake Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This study reviews the Sneaky Snake Algorithm developed by researchers at ETH University, Zurich. The paper examines the implementation and performance optimization of the Sneaky Snake algorithm, a pre-alignment filtering technique used to speed up the genome sequence analysis across various computing platforms including multicore Central Porcessing Units(CPUs), Field Programmable Gate Arrays(FPGAs), and Cloud Systems. Sneaky Snake has been designed to reduce the Approximate String Matching (ASM) problem by mapping it to Single Net Routing (SNR) problem, a common challenge in VLSI design. As a result of this Sneaky Snake provides a significant reduction in computational demand. Its application in heterogeneous computing environments was explored, utilizing OpenMP for parallel processing on CPUs, adapting the algorithm for FPGA architectures, and deploying on a cloud platform using Microsoft Azure. Performance assessments across these platforms showed marked improvements in execution times and resource efficiency, demonstrating the flexibility and scalability of Sneaky Snake in handling genomic data. This cross-platform feasibility highlights the potential of adaptive algorithms in advancing bioinformatics and genomic research, offering a versatile tool for rapid and accurate genome analysis.

articleTitle: Multi-Fidelity Aerodynamic Shape Optimization Strategies: Minimizing Induced Drag and Achieving Desired Lift Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This paper presents a novel, automated tool for optimizing aircraft wing aerodynamics using the software OpenVSP. This research emphasizes automation, eliminating the need for manual datasets, and providing a flexible solution adaptable to various aerodynamic constraints. The tool integrates a multi-objective Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm, enhanced with genetic algorithm techniques, to minimize induced drag and achieve target lift distributions within user-defined constraints. Initial results show significant reductions in induced drag and improvements in aerodynamic efficiency.

articleTitle: Delineation of the Atrial Chamber from the Cardiac Pool
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Measurements of the left atrium are key indicators for aprior prediction of heart disease. The intricate and complex nature of cardiac anatomy necessitates precise segmentation. This work presents a deep learning based methodology for left atrial segmentation in cardiac MRI for reliable automatic segmentation of the left atrium appendage. Inspired by recent advancements in medical image analysis, the approach proposes a deep learning architecture designed to enhance prediction accuracy. The results are evaluated using standard performance metrics, showcasing effectiveness and reliability of the technique. The study investigates and caters to the unique challenges posed within cardiac MRI data. It contributes to the continual evolution of medical image segmentation, ensuring a heartbeat closer to more accurate and clinically impactful diagnoses.

articleTitle: Dynamic Inversion Based Higher Order Model Reference Adaptive Control of Scalar Systems with Time Varying Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Dynamic Inversion is a promising control scheme, especially for systems with large parametric variations and high nonlinearities. In aerospace control, it is usually used to control aircraft with large flight envelope and highly nonlinear aerodynamics. Traditionally, this was catered for by using Gain Scheduling, which is a time consuming process. One major disadvantage of Dynamic Inversion is that it requires precise knowledge of system dynamics and parameters. To overcome this, some adaptation scheme could be used to estimate the parameters and uncertainties online. Model Reference Adaptive Control (MRAC) is a widely used adaptive control method in such scenarios. Conventionally, MRAC operates under the assumption that the reference or desired dynamics mirror those of the system. Yet, Dynamic Inversion transcends this constraint, often necessitating desired dynamics of higher order than that of the system itself. In this paper, we derive MRAC control laws accommodating higher order desired dynamics, for scalar systems with constant parameters. Subsequently, we extend this framework to systems featuring time-varying parameters, leveraging the concept of congelation of variables. We then apply these proposed control laws to tackle a pertinent pitch control problem, followed by simulation results and discussion.

articleTitle: IMA- An Intelligent Obfuscated Malware Analysis Model
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In the dominion of cyber-world and cybersecurity, the pervasive presence of the malware, exchanging vast amounts of data daily, has inflicted considerable harm globally, victimizing millions. Among the various manifestations of malware, obfuscation presents a unique challenge, often eluding traditional detection methods and persisting in the real world. Despite substantial efforts in this domain, existing works exhibit room for advancement, particularly with recent extensions. However, both of these existing classification methods are yet to be applied in a hybrid classification model. This work proposes a novel hybrid obfuscated malware detection model called IMA (Improved Machine-Aided) using a stacked ensemble learning process. The first layer employs the conventional machine learning processes and algorithms, i.e. Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XgBoost) Classifier, and Extremely Randomized Trees Classifier (ExtraTrees), whereas a deep learning layer refines the classification. Feature selection is done by using Pearson correlation analysis for better efficiency. Selection of an optimal feature subset optimises the classification accuracy of the model. Specifically, for the multiclass classification, the time complexity is improved by more than two times, and in the binary classifications, by more than three times. Performance evaluation is carried out on the publicly available obfuscated malware classification dataset from CIC-MaIMem-2022. The results demonstrated that the proposed IMA model could outperform other classifications.

articleTitle: VIV & Heat Transfer for Flow Around a Square Cylinder with Corner Modifications at Low Re
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The flow-induced vibrations and heat transfer properties around a square cylinder with altered corners are examined through numerical analysis to examine thermo-fluid performance. Water is utilized as the working fluid for two-dimensional (2D) simulations at a Reynolds number of 100, for a laminar flow past both sharp and chamfered cornered square cylinders. The study numerically investigates the impact of modifying the chamfer edge sizes and corner cut angles (10°, 20°, 30°, 40°, and 45°) on forced convection heat transfer from a vibrating square cylinder that is suspended elastically. The simulations are carried out with a reduced velocity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{U}_{\mathbf{red}}=\boldsymbol{6})$</tex>, considering variations in chamfer edge sizes and corner cut angles. The analyses are conducted maintaining constant values of the Prandtl number at 7.1, Reduced mass at 2, and a damping coefficient, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\xi}=\boldsymbol{0}$</tex>. The findings are presented in terms of the average drag coefficient, fluctuating values of both lift and drag coefficients, the Strouhal number and cylinder's motion trajectories. Additionally, the average Nusselt number, Nu(avg), is shown to highlight the heat transfer features surrounding the square cylinder with modified corners. The study explores the effect of corner modifications on the average drag and vorticity strength predominantly. Average drag decreases for small angular modifications but increases for larger cut angles due to an increase in the shear layer velocity and accompanying large wake recirculation bubble. Average Nusselt number increases to a maximum for the case of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{C}^{*}=\boldsymbol{0.5}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\theta}=\boldsymbol{45}^{\circ}$</tex>.

articleTitle: AI-Driven APT Detection Framework: Early Threat Identification Using ML
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: An increasing number of hacktivists, state-sponsored hackers, cybercriminals, cyber terrorists, cyber spies, and cyberwarfare warfighters are attacking the systems. A balance between real-time cyberattack detection, cyber threat intelligence, and, most importantly, cyber early warning capability is needed for a successful cyber security strategy. Cyber threats are tough and complex to describe since it is challenging to pinpoint the origin of the attack. The motivation driving them, or even to forecast how the attack will play out in real-time. The challenge of drawing boundaries between national or international, public or private objectives makes it more difficult to identify cyber threats. The fight to counteract cyber threats is dynamic and ever more difficult because they are worldwide in scope and entail quick technological advancements. In this study, we focused on the cyber-kill chain, proposed a universal/generic cyber-kill chain model, and analyzed various Advanced Persistent Threat(APT) cyber-kill chain steps/concepts. We focused on the detection of Advanced Persistent Threats by using different machine-learning models like XGBoost, Random Forest, Decision tree, Adatboost, and K-Nearest Neigbor in real-time and achieved an accuracy of 99.95% by using the model of XGBoost.

articleTitle: Enhancing the UAV Localization Accuracy by Removing False Matches Using Affine Consistency
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) face significant challenges in localization within Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) denied environments, where traditional methods often produce false matches during image matching. This paper introduces a novel approach that integrates affine consistency with flight path verification to enhance image localization accuracy. By applying affine transformations, we initially reduce false matches, but residual inaccuracies remain. To address these, our method incorporates flight path data and flight headings, to further refine the matching process. Experimental results demonstrate a substantial reduction in false matches across diverse terrains, using images sourced from Google Maps and Bing Maps. The proposed approach achieved a zero false positive rate in all tested areas, including challenging regions such as a desert area with homogeneous and less distinct terrain features. The results highlight the efficacy of our methodology in improving UAV localization accuracy, making it a robust solution for GNSS-denied environments.

articleTitle: Kernel Fashion Context Recommender System (KFCR): A Kernel Mapping Fashion Recommender System Algorithm Using Contextual Information
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In Fashion, Recommender System represents a growing trend. They enable to offer the customer online fully personalized shopping experience. Many known names on the Fashion market such as Asos (asos.com) or Zalando (zalando.com), have already bet on this technology to retain customers, boosting profits. Multiple filtering approaches exist, developed to cope with all the inherent challenges driven by the lack of information and the ephemeral nature of fashion items. However, even if the methods adopted are very varied, the main motive remains the same: reducing the margin of error at all costs to produce the nearest reality prediction. Accuracy, scalability, flexibility, and performance have become the keywords when creating a fully skilled Recommender System. To achieve these objectives, it appears that including in the model user's context information, such as time, location, mood, occasion, weather, or people's influence can be the answer. Not including contextual information is eluding a fundamental element in the decision-making process for the purchase of a particular piece of clothing. In this paper, we decided to apply to the Fashion domain issues the scalable context-aware algorithm to target the customer's tastes better, producing predictions as close to his preferences as possible. This new algorithm named KFCR uses the kernel mapping framework developed by (KMR) to complement context information. We evaluated and compared this new system to the Basic KMR, as well as to other widely used context-aware approaches like preand post-filtering techniques. Once evaluated, the KFCR was more accurate than both non-context-aware and context-aware approaches.

articleTitle: Integration of Reinforcement Learning in Industrial Pick-and-Place Robotics
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Industrial robots have significantly transformed manufacturing processes and are increasingly revolutionizing sectors such as logistics, healthcare, agriculture, and construction by enhancing efficiency, quality, and safety, making them indispensable tools for modern industries. Industrial pick-and-place robotics, while significantly advancing, still faces several challenges like Object variability, Environmental factors, Task complexity, Precision and speed. Reinforcement learning (RL) offers a transformative approach to industrial pick-and-place robotics, addressing the limitations of traditional, pre-programmed methods. In order to overcome these challenges, the present research explores how reinforcement learning (RL) may assist robots to determine optimal picking and placing techniques without requiring explicit programming. We developed a framework that employs deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to create an autonomous pick-and-place system. Using Gazebo and ROS, we designed a simulated environment where the robotic arm is trained with Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and Deep Q-Network (DQN) algorithms.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis for CSI, QoS, and Hybrid SIC Based Decoding Order Schemes in NOMA-Assisted MEC Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) emerges as a pivotal technology in 5G networks, primarily due to its dual-core components: Superposition Coding (SC) and Successive Interference Cancellation (SIC). These elements enable the concurrent transmission of signals from multiple users over the same time and frequency. This paper demonstrates a thorough comparative analysis of various SIC order schemes in NOMA systems. The discussed schemes include Quality of Service (QoS) based, Channel State Information (CSI) based and Hybrid SIC schemes. This paper highlights the performance differences of these decoding order schemes in NOMA-MEC systems, as well as their applications. To be specific, the Bit Error Rate vs SNR, The Outage Probability vs SNR and the Sum Data Rate vs SNR are discussed in three different SIC schemes and it was found that Hybrid SIC has better performance.

articleTitle: Detailed Analysis on the Micro-Architecture and Integration of Bit Manipulation Extensions in the SweRV EH1 Core of a RISC-V Processor and its Functional Verification
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Embedded system applications and small electronic devices demand cost-effective, high-performance, energy-efficient, and secure processor architectures. In this context, RISC-V has emerged as a significant competitor to conventional architectures like Intel x86 and ARM, particularly in embedded systems and Internet of Things (IoT) applications. The SweRV EH1 core, based on the RISC-V architecture, is specifically designed to meet these demands. In this work, we perform a detailed analysis of the existing SweRV EH1 core microarchitecture and integrate bit manipulation extensions that support low-power embedded applications. The detailed microarchitecture of the SweRV EH1 core is designed and explained, including the bit manipulation extensions. The improved microarchitecture is later tested using Verilator. The results show that the SweRV EH1 core with new bit manipulation extensions improves performance, reduces code density, and enhances power usage efficiency. This contributes to the ongoing research on the RISC-V architecture and provides insights into the benefits of integrating bit manipulation extensions in embedded systems.

articleTitle: Prediction of Low Velocity Impact Performance of Carbon/Flax Bio-Hybrid Composites Using Experimental and Neural Network Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In this paper., the effect of fiber hybridization and stacking configurations on the low-velocity impact behavior of carbon/flax bio-hybrid composite laminates was investigated. The methodology was developed based on experimental testing and then utilizing an artificial neural network-based machine learning regression model. Five different stacking configurations of carbon/flax material were manufactured using the vacuum bagging method and then subjected to low-velocity impact with impact energies ranging from 15J to 90J. Data in the form of peak impact force was recorded for each stacking configuration. A symmetric configuration with a uniform distribution of flax layers across the thickness exhibited enhanced performance. Two machine learning approaches—deep neural network (DNN) with Adam optimizer and DNN with stochastic gradient descent (SGD)—were applied. The performance metrics used to evaluate the performance were the coefficient of determination <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{R}^{2})$</tex>, mean square error (MSE)., and mean absolute error (MAE). The best-performing model for the prediction of peak impact force was DNN-SGD., with three hidden layers and 80 neurons in each hidden layer. The highest correlation and the smallest MSE and MAE values were attained using the DNN-SGD model. The developed methodology and the model serve as powerful tools for the prediction of the mechanical properties of bio-hybrid composite laminates., utilizing minimal resources and saving time as well.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning-Based Framework for Predicting E-Commerce Product Ratings
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Big data has been the center of attention for industry due to the volume of data that is being generated and growing over time. Machine learning algorithms are being employed more and more to anticipate various features of products. Product ratings are one of the key metrics used by every firm to evaluate the performance of its products. The product rating methodology persuades customers to purchase any item. It also demonstrates a product's potential for success in the consumer market. In order to forecast a product's rating based on its category, listed price, reduced price, and number of ratings, this study used a machine learning model. The Amazon dataset, which is accessible on Kaggle, was used in this study. This study evaluates various machine learning models using a dataset of 61,950 electronics appliance entries from Amazon to predict product ratings based on category, listed price, reduced price, and number of ratings. The Random Forest model outperforms others, with a precision of 0.65 and recall of 0.6 for 1-star ratings, and demonstrates superior performance for 2-star, 4-star, and 5-star predictions.

articleTitle: Assessing Concept Drift in Malware: A Comprehensive Review and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The rapid evolution of malware has been posing substantial challenges for conventional detection systems due to attackers' continuous adaptations to evade detection. Concept drift, characterized by the changing statistical properties of data over time, is critical in understanding malware dynamics. A comprehensive dataset of Portable Executable (PE) malware samples spanning various families was analyzed to assess the overall drift in malware characteristics. Static features were utilized to delineate the structural and behavioral attributes of malware, ensuring early detection and resource efficiency. Robust clustering techniques were employed to facilitate the identification of evolving patterns and trends from 2017 to 2023. The analysis quantifies the extent of concept drift, highlighting the necessity for adaptive detection mechanisms to effectively combat emerging malware threats. The results indicate significant deviations among malware clusters over the years, highlighting significant concept drift. The findings underscore the dynamic nature of malware across different families and its impact on detection systems. The study emphasizes the necessity for detection frameworks that are capable of adapting to temporal variations and emerging threats.

articleTitle: Minimizing Soil Mineralization Effects in Pulse Induced Metal Detector Through Dual Adaptive Filter-Based Compensation to Detect Low Metal Contents
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: De-mining operations are crucial for humanitarian efforts and safety in conflict-affected regions. As conflicts persist, so do advancements in technology and the challenges they present, particularly with landmines containing very low or sub-gram metal contents. In this paper, we address the challenge of improving the accuracy of mine detection systems in mineralized soil. We present a novel algorithm based on dual adaptive filters to compensate the effect of soil mineralization. The filters learn the response of the mineralization content within the ground through supervised learning and remove the effects with a high degree of confidence (above 98%). The paper also considers a challenging mineralized environment containing the baked clay bricks and shows the effectiveness of the presented dual adaptive filter-based compensation (DAFC) algorithm for it. The parametric approach used in the algorithm also provides a way to reduce the effect of over compensation in real-time.

articleTitle: MASA: Multi Agent Situational Awareness for Visually Impaired
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Visually impaired people (VIP) face difficulties in perceiving and comprehending their surroundings and, there-fore, feel disconnected from the environment. Due to visionary challenges, VIPs face challenges in carrying out routine activities but are also prone to possible risks and hazards in dynamic environments. A number of recent studies have proposed solutions for VIP based on different types of sensors and machine learning algorithms. But previously proposed systems lack an all-in-one wearable solution for visually impaired people due to rigorous training requirements for each scenario, and no conditional outputs based on user queries. In this research, we propose a novel solution named MASA for VIPs. MASA is a wearable solution for situational awareness and dynamic decision-making based on visual sensor and user queries. The proposed framework leverages vision language models (VLMs) and employs an agentic workflow for VLMs to reduce user cognitive overloading by removing all redundant information from the final output. The solution is deployed on a customized VR headset, which has Raspberry Pi, batteries, camera fitted into it. For evaluation purposes, 20 healthy subjects with good vision used MASA in 10 different scenarios. Qualitative feedback from the 20 subjects yielded encouraging results. Quantitative analysis was conducted using human-defined baselines.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Anomaly Detection for Man-in-the-Middle Attack Identification in Cloud Computing Infrastructures
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Cloud computing is rapidly provisioning resources within a computer system, particularly processing power and data storage, without requiring direct user administration. Cyberattacks known as MITM (Man in the Middle) attacks occur when an attacker eavesdrops on communication between a client and a cloud server. The objective of a Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attack is not only to obtain the victim's private data. Breach of confidentiality as per the data can be accomplished by intercepting, replaying, and modulation of the communication between the parties, especially to modify the data and gain unauthorized access to the systems involved. The attack can enable a host of undesirable actions, which range from identity theft, financial scams, and social disorder. Due to their extraordinary ingenuity, these network defects persist and obstruct safe traffic. the attackers alter their conduct dynamically to avoid detection. Critical aspects of cloud computing, such as man-in-the-middle attacks (MITM), are examined in this research, and a machine learning model utilizing K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), Random Forest (RF), and Support Vector Machine (SVM) is being constructed to effectively identify these attacks. XG Boost is used to Train the model for better detection for selected features These models apply the existing datasets, and the result show an accuracy of 99. 17%”. %.

articleTitle: ServeNet-GPT-Fusion: A Fusion Language Model For Web Services Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Automatic service classification plays an important role in service discovery, selection, and composition. Recently, machine learning has been widely used in service classification. Even though promising results are obtained, previous methods in a small-scale dataset has reached its limit. In this paper, we propose a method that integrates with existing large language models to further enhance the prediction accuracy across 50 service categories. To demonstrate the efficiency of our approach, we conducted experiments on predicting classification accuracy across 50 service categories using three ChatGPT models. The results indicated that each of the three ChatGPT's are prominent at predicting different service categories compared to existing results. By further integrating existing outcomes with these three models through a weighted voting method, we achieved a further improvement in accuracy.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Pole Placement and Linear Quadratic Controller for Above Knee Prosthetic Leg
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Lower limb prostheses are the basic requirement of amputees who have lost their limbs due to the war, accidents, natural disasters and any other physiological or motor system disorder. People with lower-limb amputations have remained the major concern among them. In this regard, researchers have designed different prosthetic limbs with various control strategies. Prosthetics can be grouped in two types on the basis of their working as active and passive. The focus of this research was to make active lower limb prostheses that imitate the motion of the real limb. This research is held for finding the mathematical model and simulation of above-knee prosthetic (AKP) for lower limb amputees. The transfer function and state-space model for 3 DOF AKP has been simulated using Simulink in MATLAB®. Controllability and observability of the model have been computed. Further, pole placement (non-optimal) and linear-quadratic (LQ) controller has been designed and compared for the system to control the motion of the AKP leg. The results show that optimal and robust controllers provide desired stability and control of the prosthetic by providing minimum energy.

articleTitle: Accuracy Enhancing Time Limited Model Reduction Framework: Computational Efficiency in Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The analytical and modelling precision required to build modern wind turbines makes them stable, controlled, and observable. This article presents a state-of-the-art method for lowering the model order of a wind turbine driven by a double-fed induction generator, where the rotational speed varies over time. The suggested approach uses state-space representations to set up a comprehensive and systematic framework for analysing wind turbine performance and checking for compliance with grid standards. A time-constrained Gramians-based novel balanced realization approach is employed to reduce the dimensionality of the large-scale wind turbine model. Stability and reduced approximation error are two benefits of the lower-order system. The proposed method also gives researchers an a priori formula for the error-bound, making computations faster and more efficient. Using substantial simulation data, we show that our method improves upon previous methods in optimising models that include wind turbines with changing rotational speeds, taking into account both stability and error computation. To enhance the efficacy and accuracy of their modeling procedures, academics and researchers analyzing wind turbines should incorporate this new methodology.

articleTitle: Layered Double Hydroxide Based Self-Powered Triboelectric Sensor for Biomechanical Motions
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Sensing of biomechanical motions is advantageous for biomedical health monitoring. Here, we propose a layered double hydroxide (LDH) based triboelectric sensor (TES) for monitoring biomechanical motions. The triboelectric sensor is based on initially triboelectrification between the friction pair of LDH and aluminum and subsequently electrostatic induction in an external electric circuit due to the contact-separation of the two friction layers. To realize the triboelectric sensor, ZnAl-LDH is synthesized using an in-situ hydrothermal method resulting in a nanostructured ZnAl-LDH with high surface-to-volume ratio. The triboelectric sensor is self-powered as it generates a peak-to-peak output voltage (Vo) of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 11$</tex> V across a load resistance of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\mathrm{M}\Omega$</tex> and a short circuit current (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SC</inf>) of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 2.5\mu\mathrm{A}$</tex> in response to hand tapping. Since the triboelectric pulses (high voltages and very low currents) are not suited for conventional electronics, a two-stage-amplifier based interface circuit is designed to interface the sensor to a microcontroller. As proof of concept, the self-powered triboelectric sensor is interfaced with Arduino Mega 2560 microcontroller through the interface circuit. The sensorial system monitored the contact-separation induced by hand tapping and the counting information was displayed on a digital LCD. The self-powered LDH based triboelectric sensor along with the two-stage-amplifier based interface circuit provides a platform for monitoring various biomechanical motions including walking with applications in biomedical health monitoring.

articleTitle: The Effect of Affine and Extended Affine Equivalence Class Against Various Cryptographic Profile
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: S-boxes play a crucial role in various symmetric primitives by substituting a certain number of input bits in a nonlinear way to achieve optimal security bounds. To attain these optimal security bounds, researchers explore the Affine and Extended Affine (EA) equivalence classes. In this research, we investigate the effect of Affine and EA equivalence classes on different Cryptographic Properties (CPs). CPs like Differential Uniformity (DU), Algebraic Degree (AD), Strict Avalanche Criterion (SAC), Nonlinearity (NL), Autocorrelation (AC), and Linear Structure (LS) remain invariant under Affine and EA transformations, while other cryptographic properties like Branch Number (BN), Number of Terms in Interpolation Polynomials (NIP), bijectivity, Side Channel Profile (SCP), and some hybrid CPs are not preserved under the EA class. These results highlight the importance of careful selection of Affine and EA parameters during the design process to achieve strong resistance against a range of statistical and differential attacks.

articleTitle: Adaptive Power Control Based on Neural Network Design and Implementation for the Hybrid Shipboard Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: With the increase in carbon emissions, climate change, and reduction in fossil fuels, there is a need for energy storage systems and renewable energy sources for ships and ferries. Currently, seaports do not have shore-based cold ironing facilities in most ship ports. Therefore, electricity is provided by the main grid. Due to the lack of a cold ironing facility on the ship, expansive diesel generators must be equipped on the ship. Furthermore, the ship must be functional to provide supply to auxiliary loads on the ship. To provide a solution to these issues, we need to provide cold ironing facilities to every seaport. However, this solution will take time to implement, and it will be very costly. On the other hand, ship-based microgrid systems will enable clean and economical power generation facilities on the ship. The idea is to implement a low-cost hybrid microgrid system on the ship so that we receive alternate energy resources. We proposed a nonlinear droop control design for the improvement of voltage and frequency droops in the bidirectional power converter model. A comparison of conventional and proposed control designs has been presented in simulation results. Hard-ware implementation on the Jetson Nano system and practical results have been validated.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Improved Soft Magnetic Composites (SMCs) for Applications in Transformer Core
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This study investigates the synthesis of Ni-Zn ferrite (Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>Zn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>) and Ni-Zn-Co ferrite <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\left(\text{Ni}_{0.3} \text{Zn}_{0.5} \text{Co}_{0.2} \text{Fe}_2 \mathrm{O}_4\right)$</tex> cores via ball milling method for the transformers operating in the frequency range of 0.1 kHz to 100 kHz. Ni-Zn ferrite cores were synthesized using <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Fe}2\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Fe}3\mathrm{O}_{4}$</tex> as primary raw materials and Ni-Zn-Co ferrite was prepared using <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Fe}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$</tex> as raw material. The magnetic, structural and morphological properties were characterized using vibrating sample magnetometry (VSM), X-ray diffraction (XRD) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) respectively. Results demonstrated that the Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>Zn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> ferrite core synthesized with Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> exhibits superior magnetic properties, maintaining stability across a frequency range of 0.1 kHz to 100 kHz and a temperature range of 10 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^\circ\mathrm{C}$</tex> to 40 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{oC}$</tex>. Both Ni-Zn ferrite and Ni-Zn-Co ferrite cores showed promising stability, making them suitable for high-frequency transformer applications.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Robust Control Solutions for Buck Converters: ANN and Fuzzy Logic Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Machine learning (ML) techniques are increasingly explored in power electronics converters for enhancing control solutions. This study investigates robust control for buck converters using Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), Fuzzy Logic Control (FLC), and Model Predictive Control (MPC). Implemented in MATLAB Simulink, four scenarios were considered: Open Loop Buck Converter (OLBC), Fuzzy Logic Controller-Based Buck Converter (FLBC), ANN-Based Buck Converter (ANNBC), and MPC-Based Buck Converter (MPCBC). Performance metrics such as rise time, settling time, overshoot, and peak values were evaluated under various input voltages and load conditions. Results demonstrate that ANN-based control significantly outperforms other methods, with ANNBC achieving an extremely low overshoot of 0.0781 %, compared to 57.7626% for OLBC, 47.8383% for FLBC, and 105.3098% for MPCBC. ANNBC also maintained robust performance with minimal variations in rise time, settling time, and peak values across different conditions. Despite a longer rise time and settling time compared to some techniques, ANNBC's precision, stability, and robustness justify this tradeoff. The study highlights that while MPCBC offers effective control, it exhibits higher overshoot and longer settling time compared to ANNBC. This study underscores the potential of ML, particularly ANN, in providing robust and high-precision control for buck converters, making it preferable for demanding applications.

articleTitle: State-of-the-Art Multi-Core Architectures: Analyzing Current Research, Identifying Gaps, and Exploring Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Multi-core architectures in modern computing systems are constantly being improved by focusing on enhancing their energy efficiency, performance, and security. This study aims at investigating how multi-core architectures affect computational workloads, addressing scalability problems as well as suggesting novel optimization strategies. In this article, we assessed Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC) algorithm's performance using a fine-grained and coarse grained parallelism approach on a multicores Intel Xeon E5-2680 processor. Further, the study evaluated the HeteroCore GPU architecture for optimized multitasking and explored deterministic memory hierarchy for predictable access patterns. Key findings indicate that multi-core architectures improve performance through parallel processing and also save energy despite challenges such as software complexity or memory bandwidth limitations. For instance, fine-grained parallelism resulted in significant speedup in CRC algorithms whereas adaptive thermal management techniques reduced processor temperature which enhanced reliability. This analysis emphasizes efficient resource allocation mechanisms, time verification plus thermal management to optimize multicore performance. The study concludes with possible future directions including further optimizing of parallelism techniques and exploration of security measures in multi-core systems.

articleTitle: Real-Time VoIP Classification in Encrypted Traffic Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: With over 95% of internet traffic now encrypted, traditional methods like Deep Packet Inspection (DPI) and payload-based classification have been rendered ineffective. This study investigates the application of deep learning for real-time Voice over IP (VoIP) classification in encrypted network traffic. The ineffectiveness of traditional methods motivates the exploration of deep learning models, including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), and 1D Convolutional Neural Network (1D-CNN). This work leverages the pattern recognition power of deep learning to classify internet traffic as either VoIP or non-VOIP. The study includes improving data diversification by collecting and integrating network traces of VoIP and non-VoIP traffic from different origins. Furthermore, the efficacy of manual and automatic feature extraction techniques is comparatively evaluated. The findings demonstrate that manually extracted features yield superior classification accuracy. Manual feature extraction resulted in LSTM, MLP, and ID-CNN accuracy rates of 94.7%, 94.8%, and 67.5%, respectively. Automatic feature extraction yielded 73.1%, 71.6%, and 41.5%. Notably, the MLP model achieves the highest accuracy (94.8%) while maintaining significantly faster classification times. This efficiency makes it well-suited for real-time VoIP classification.

articleTitle: A Password Strength Classifier Using Supervised Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Having a strong password is one of the basic protections one can have against identity theft and hacking. Yet, data gathered about annual security breaches suggests that accounts being compromised due to weak passwords amounts to about 61% of all security breaches. Polls and surveys conducted in first world countries show us that a vast majority of users do not frequently reset their passwords, reuse passwords across multiple sites and keep weak passwords to begin with. This scenario will be even worse in countries like ours where technical knowledge among the general public is limited. Through this work, we aim to make a password classifier which would tell the users the strength of their entered passwords, thereby, highlighting any potential weaknesses in their passwords. Here, we have used multiple classifier models to test the strength of passwords including Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes, KNN, Random Forest and XGBoost. Their performance metrics are tested and a maximum accuracy of 0.9933 is achieved along with a Matthew's Correlation Coefficient of 0.99. XGBoost is selected a the best-performing classifier for this case. With highest value of accuracy (0.9933), Matthew's Correlation Coefficient (0.99) and AUC (0.9953). To cater the need for strong passwords, we also proposed a password generator that generates strong password.

articleTitle: Anomaly Detection in HTTP Logs: Leveraging Machine Learning for Uncovering Anomalous Traffic Patterns with SIEM Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Network traffic continuously rises, and network services become increasingly more complex and vulnerable. Intrusion detection systems are employed to safeguard these networks. Signature-based intrusion detection cannot detect new attacks, so anomaly detection is necessary. Also, most of the traditional security information and event management (SIEM) doesn't have any live dataset creation or anomalous data log detection. In this paper, we propose a framework for detecting anomalies in Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) logs, enabling fast detection of anomalies, visualization of network traffic, and integration with SIEM solutions. This solution gets HTTP logs from the network and preprocesses them. Then, the solution checks the traffic for anomaly detection by applying the Isolation Forest algorithm using unsupervised learning. Later, we will then explore those anomalies with clustering using the K-means method. The proposed solution uses no predefined dataset file. But, it trains on the live data logs, where the user checks for any anomalous data logs within a given timestamp. The logs from this specified timestamp serve as the dataset for the model's training. The solutions are on live network HTTP logs, but in this paper, we are using this solution on a test network where we have 153 logs, of which 32 are declared anomalous by our proposed solution and after that the clustering on those anomalous data logs were applied. Finally, the results are sent to the SIEM solution, which visualizes the network and the anomalous traffic. Besides this, the solution is quick to detect intrusion attempts. This method is significant in the sense, that because it contributes to proactive cybersecurity strategies specifically designed to meet the requirements of Security Operations Center (SOC) analysts and threat-hunting teams.

articleTitle: Analysis of Hot Streak Migration Characteristics in a Transonic Turbine Employing Nonlinear Harmonic Method
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The migration characteristics of the hot streak (HS) are critical to analyze for the turbine designers to optimize the blade cooling schemes during design phase. Numerical investigations of the HS migration characteristics in a highly loaded transonic turbine have been conducted employing the Nonlinear Harmonic (NLH) method and unsteady RANS. The NLH method using three harmonics has effectively captured the hot streak characteristics with about 7 times less computationally expensive than the unsteady RANS. Two HS clocking positions relative to the stator leading edge (impinging and non-impinging) have been investigated. The turbine efficiency decreases by increasing HS temperature ratio however; the HS clocking position has no significant impact on the efficiency. The radial distribution of the HS remains unaffected through the stator passage however; the HS core temperature drop for impinging case is relatively higher than non-impinging case. The radial distribution of the HS through the rotor passage shows that the radial amplitude of the HS total temperature distortion decays more in the impinging case. The buoyancy force is found to be mainly responsible for radial migration of the HS towards the rotor hub which is directly proportionate to the HS temperature ratio and inversely proportionate to the square of the flow coefficient. The analysis of unsteady rotor surface temperature fluctuations shows that the rotor pressure side bears higher fluctuations for both clocking positions however the time averaged temperature envelop is compact and a balanced thermal load is achieved between the pressure side and suction side for the impinging case. The instantaneous entropy distribution and the time-space plots of total temperature distribution have shown the phenomenon of preferential heating on the rotor pressure side for non-impinging case. The rotor vortex shedding frequency remains unaffected of the HS clocking position as well as the HS temperature ratio. The NLH method has shown remarkable advantage over unsteady RANS in terms of computational cost with comparable results thus offering an opportunity for the designers to imply unsteady computations during design phase.

articleTitle: Enhanced Pneumothorax Detection in Chest Radiographs via a Deep Learning Framework DENSE Network Fusion with Yolov8
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Pneumothorax (PTX, sometimes called collapsed lung, is a condition where air is trapped between the chest cavity and the lung. Human breathlessness is a potentially fatal condition known as pneumothorax. Every year, 1.88 million individuals pass away with pneumothorax. To diagnose PTX, chest radiographs, or CXRs, are utilized. Pneumothorax may be diagnosed by X-ray scans, which are a rapid, easy, and affordable procedure that is utilized in hospitals worldwide. The lack of skilled physicians and radiologists is the reason for the need for a technology that identifies PTX from X-ray images at advanced medical institutions. Professionals find it more challenging to handle manually, but it may be resolved automatically, simplifying the medical procedure. This paper proposes a framework for the automated and efficient diagnosis of pneumothorax from CXR utilizing a dense detection algorithm and pretrained YOLOv8. With a 98.72% accuracy rate, our system categorized CXRs as either PTX or healthy. The YOLOv8 detection method and the DensetNet-201 model fused increase classification performance while cutting down on training test time. There is a good chance that the suggested framework will be useful in helping medical professionals diagnose lung diseases.

articleTitle: Determination of Activation Energy Using Various Kinetic Models and Their Influence on Life Prediction of Neoprene Rubber
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Determination of kinetic parameter (activation energy, E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>) is crucial in the field of fabrication, material synthesis, bio-medicals, catalysis, and many other industrial production to understand the processes like curing, thermal decomposition, crystallization and solid state transformation etc. To obtain kinetic parameters, a number of kinetic methods employing non-isothermal techniques have been devised. The main objective of this study is to investigate the consequences of various non-isothermal methods on activation energy of neoprene rubber and their impact on life prediction using ASTM E 1877. All polymers possess inherent vulnerability to oxidation, a basic process that is responsible for material deterioration overtime. Kinetic models are intended to delineate the reaction mechanisms and reaction rates, while swift qualification testing aim to establish confidence in prolonged performance during service operation. It is indispensable to assess the aging effects of extended duration at room temperature on elastomeric parts like shock isolators, O-rings etc. To comprehend this impact, accelerated thermal aging at elevated temperature (100°C for 72 hours, 144 hours and 216 hours) was investigated. This research study also delves the effect of accelerated thermal aging on the activation energy values of neoprene rubber. Determining this kinetic parameter for elastomeric material like neoprene using elongation, tensile strength, tensile modulus is both expensive and time consuming. A substitute method implicates analyzing the weight loss kinetics by Thermo Gravimetric Analysis (TGA) utilizing model free kinetics such as Flynn-Wall-Ozawa (FWO), Kissinger-Akahira-Sunose (KAS) and Kissinger methods. This tactic is appealing because of the readily accessibility to require instrumentation and software. To ascertain the variations in the activation energy for thermo-oxidative degradation under temperature variable conditions, thermal analysis using (TGA) was carried out at different heating rates (5, 7, 10 K/min) within temperature range of 25°C to 700°C. It was revealed that activation energy obtained changes with the extent of thermal degradation. Additionally, using Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy structural changes were investigated, this study revealed that aging is associated with significant oxidation.

articleTitle: Flight Mechanics of a Supersonic Projectile: A Parametric Investigation
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The stability coefficients and derivatives are used to determine a vehicle's motion and are considered critical for the design of flight vehicles. In this research, the dynamic pitch derivatives of an axisymmetric projectile prototype are examined using Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD). For this purpose, a methodology is established by validating two test cases and then applied to a newly designed prototype. The dynamic damping derivatives are calculated using the forced oscillation approach. The pitch damping coefficients are simulated for angles of attack from 0° to 20°. A decent agreement is observed between the CFD and experimental data. The test cases are also analyzed through DATCOM for comparative analysis. A conceptual projectile geometry is designed and evaluated at a Mach number of 1.5. A parametric analysis is also conducted for the variation of Mach number and reduced pitch rate on pitch damping coefficients for the conceptual geometry. This study establishes the use of CFD to determine fast and consistent estimates for the aerodynamic stability parameters.

articleTitle: Robust Battery Management System for UAV Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: UAVs have become indispensable tools in agriculture, disaster management, surveillance and filmmaking. This study presents an advanced Battery Management System (BMS) designed explicitly for drone/UAV applications, with a primary objective of achieving Technology Readiness Level 4 (TRL4) certification. The BMS incorporates critical safety modes such as Undervoltage Lockout (UVLO) and Ship mode, ensuring operational excellence and safety across various scenarios. Among its features are customisable charging/discharging voltage ranges and programmable timings, offering unparalleled adaptability to meet the dynamic demands of diverse missions. Furthermore, integrating a watchdog mechanism significantly enhances system reliability and resilience, guaranteeing sustained performance even in adverse conditions. Leveraging an accessible I2C interface, the BMS enables real-time monitoring of cell voltages, state of charge (SoC), and temperature, furnishing operators with indispensable insights into battery health and operational performance. This design is extensively tested to international standards to achieve a highly reliable product.

articleTitle: A Numerical Approach to Predict Roller Follower Valve Trian Frictional Torque Considering the Effects of Roller Sliding
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The efficiency and reliability of engine parts are largely governed by friction. The valve train assembly is considered one of the extremely difficult assemblies in terms of its tribological performance and is often subjected to severe and unsteady functional conditions leading towards friction and wear of components. In this research work, a comprehensive numerical approach addressing mixed lubrication theory will be presented to investigate the frictional performance of a roller follower valve train system considering the impact of roller sliding, asperity interaction and friction arising from associated components under different operating conditions. A direct relationship between total drive torque and camshaft rotational frequency has been found predicting an increase in sliding friction due to roller slip on the camshaft surface. Relatively greater magnitude of roller sliding was observed in cam flank regions resulting in high sliding friction. A rise in hydrodynamic friction was found due to the shearing of a relatively thick oil film at a low lubricant supply temperature.

articleTitle: Underwater Object Detection from Sonar Images Using Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Underwater systems are always prone to complex environmental conditions and various interferences that is the reason why Sonar images are filled up with contamination, noise, and blurriness. Collection of real-world underwater images data is very costly with respect to human resources, time, equipment and logistics. Due to these challenges, there are very few publicly available datasets of underwater sonar images and only few datasets are available for underwater images which are scarce because of lack of resources. Precise and fast detection of objects in underwater sonar images is very less explored and still an open challenge for underwater systems.
